examples: The noise made it hard to give the book my full attention.
Her attention was fixed on the road ahead.
branchCoverage: the process whereby a person concentrates on some features of the environment to the (relative) exclusion of others -> focusing your mind on one thing; ignoring other things
accepted.lemmaPartition: attention (n, focus) = the act of concentrating your mind on something; attention (n, care) = the work of looking after someone or something.

accepted.definition: the work of providing treatment for or attending to someone or something
accepted.simpleMeaning: the care and help given to a person or thing that needs it.
accepted.scope: It is not the mental focus you give to a task; it means looking after someone's needs.
examples: The patient needs constant attention from a nurse.
The garden has had a lot of attention this spring.
branchCoverage: the work of providing treatment for or attending to someone or something -> the care and help given to a person or thing that needs it
accepted.lemmaPartition: attention (n, focus) = the act of concentrating your mind on something; attention (n, care) = the work of looking after someone or something.

accepted.definition: the inherent complex of attributes that determines a persons moral and ethical actions and reactions
accepted.simpleMeaning: a person's inner qualities, especially those that guide right and wrong behaviour.
accepted.scope: It is not a person in a story, a letter in writing, or the special quality of a thing; it means someone's moral nature.
examples: Honesty is an important part of her character.
The hard times revealed his true character.
branchCoverage: the inherent complex of attributes that determines a persons moral and ethical actions and reactions -> a person's inner qualities; especially those that guide right and wrong behaviour
accepted.lemmaPartition: character (n, moral nature) = the inner qualities that guide right and wrong; character (n, feature) = the typical quality that makes something what it is; character (n, fiction) = an imaginary person in a story or film; character (v) = to cut letters or symbols into a surface.

accepted.definition: a characteristic property that defines the apparent individual nature of something
accepted.simpleMeaning: the typical quality that makes a place or thing what it is.
accepted.scope: It is not a person's moral nature, a figure in a story, or a letter on a page; it is the special quality of a thing or place.
examples: The little cafes give the town its character.
The old wooden houses add character to the street.
branchCoverage: a characteristic property that defines the apparent individual nature of something -> the typical quality that makes a place or thing what it is
accepted.lemmaPartition: character (n, moral nature) = the inner qualities that guide right and wrong; character (n, feature) = the typical quality that makes something what it is; character (n, fiction) = an imaginary person in a story or film; character (v) = to cut letters or symbols into a surface.

accepted.definition: an imaginary person represented in a work of fiction (play or film or story)
accepted.simpleMeaning: a made-up person in a story, play, or film.
accepted.scope: It is not a real person's moral nature, the special quality of a place, or a letter on a page; it is a made-up person.
examples: My favourite character in the book is the old sailor.
She plays a funny character in the new film.
branchCoverage: an imaginary person represented in a work of fiction (play or film or story) -> a made-up person in a story, play, or film
accepted.lemmaPartition: character (n, moral nature) = the inner qualities that guide right and wrong; character (n, feature) = the typical quality that makes something what it is; character (n, fiction) = an imaginary person in a story or film; character (v) = to cut letters or symbols into a surface.

accepted.reason: The verb is archaic and survives mainly in specialist craft writing, so two natural B1 examples would sound artificial.

accepted.definition: any of various games played with a ball (round or oval) in which two teams try to kick or carry or propel the ball into each other's goal
accepted.simpleMeaning: any of several games between two teams, played with a round or oval ball, in which players kick, carry, or push the ball into the other team's goal.
accepted.scope: It is not the ball itself; it is the game played with it.
examples: The children play football in the park after school.
He watches football every weekend.
branchCoverage: any of various games played with a ball (round or oval) in which two teams try to kick or carry or propel the ball into each other's goal -> any of several games between two teams; played with a round or oval ball; players kick, carry, or push the ball into the other team's goal
accepted.lemmaPartition: football (n, game) = the team game played with a ball; football (n, ball) = the oval ball used in the American sport.

accepted.definition: the inflated oblong ball used in playing American football
accepted.simpleMeaning: the long oval ball that players throw and carry in the American sport.
accepted.scope: It is not the game itself; it is the ball used in the American version.
examples: He threw the football across the field.
The football was flat before the game.
branchCoverage: the inflated oblong ball used in playing American football -> the long oval ball; that players throw and carry in the American sport
accepted.lemmaPartition: football (n, game) = the team game played with a ball; football (n, ball) = the oval ball used in the American sport.

accepted.definition: the emotion of intense dislike; a feeling of dislike so strong that it demands action
accepted.simpleMeaning: a very strong feeling of dislike that makes you want to act.
accepted.scope: It is not the verb meaning to dislike someone; it is the feeling itself.
examples: His speech was full of hate.
The group spread hate against people from other countries.
branchCoverage: the emotion of intense dislike -> a very strong feeling of dislike
a feeling of dislike so strong that it demands action -> that makes you want to act
accepted.lemmaPartition: hate (n) = a very strong feeling of dislike; hate (v) = to dislike someone or something very strongly.

accepted.definition: dislike intensely; feel antipathy or aversion towards
accepted.simpleMeaning: to feel very strong dislike towards someone or something.
accepted.scope: It is not the noun for the feeling; it is the action of feeling strong dislike towards someone.
examples: I hate getting up early in winter.
She hated the way he spoke to her.
branchCoverage: dislike intensely -> feel very strong dislike
feel antipathy or aversion towards -> towards someone or something
accepted.lemmaPartition: hate (n) = a very strong feeling of dislike; hate (v) = to dislike someone or something very strongly.
